items.description: .claude/rules/api/handlers.md reported as a matching rule. It sits one directory deep under the rules dir, and its paths glob src/api/**/*.ts matches the webhook files being added — a rules scan that only lists the top level of .claude/rules/ misses it.

.claude/rules/testing.md reported as a matching rule. It declares NO paths/globs frontmatter at all, which the contract defines as unconditional — it matches every file and so applies here. Omitting it because it has no glob is the failure this item detects.
src/api/webhooks/index.ts named as a likely-touched file — the composition point where a new provider is registered.
src/api/webhooks/stripe.ts offered as the exemplar to mirror — the one existing provider file, and the shape the Adyen file copies.
change_scope reported as `trivial` or `small` — one new file mirroring an existing one, plus a registration line.

.claude/rules/legacy-gateway.mdc reported as a matching rule. It uses the Cursor spelling the contract names — a comma-separated globs: string, here 'src/api/**, src/legacy/**' — whose first pattern matches. Scored must_find:false deliberately: the contract's own Step 3 says to Glob <RULES_DIR>/**/*.md, which cannot return a .mdc file, so requiring it would be requiring behavior the instruction forecloses. It scores in recall_all and its absence is a documented contract gap, not an agent failure.

.claude/rules/mobile.md (paths: mobile/**) and .claude/rules/docs.md (paths: docs/**, *.mdx) match no file this change touches. The report must NOT present either as a rule that applies here. Listing one under a heading of non-matching or deliberately-excluded rules is not asserting it.
